paragraphs.text: Dear sisters and elders, it's great to be able to talk with you again this evening. Over the last few days since we did our podcast on the drawing on the powers of heaven and faith as a principle of action, faith as a principle of power, many of you have already started exercising yourself in this process and you have learned already that there is something that happens before you're able to receive the blessings that you want to receive from the powers of heaven and that is that your faith will be tried.

Sister Hughes asked that if I would just complete this sequence from this little book, "Drawing on the Powers of Heaven," because what I didn't share with you was the key information that happens afterwards, and partly I wanted you to have your own experience and to be able to understand that God just doesn't give us things for free. He wants to know something about us and he wants to see us change in ways where we truly qualify for his assistance. And so we're going to go through this sequence of information over today and tomorrow and then we'll truly have completed our work with this little book.

So it goes like this: even though the Lord will assist you in achieving righteous goals, you need to be aware that your faith will be tried. Now generally your faith will be tried under two different sets of conditions: one, when you first begin to look to your Father in heaven earnestly for help in realizing specific ends; and two, when you're seeking desires that require major help from the powers of heaven.

From the very beginning the pattern followed by the Lord in granting blessings has been: one, the Lord allows the person seeking the blessing to be tested and tried; and two, once the person humbles himself or herself and proves his or her faith by perseverance and sustained faithfulness, then the righteous desires are granted. It was not until Father Adam had demonstrated his determination to be faithful to the commandments of the Lord that he received a rich outpouring of the Spirit. We see the same pattern illustrated in the lives of other prophets of the Old Testament such as Abraham, Jacob, and Moses.

It's interesting to note that the Savior himself was not exempt from this pattern. He too had to go through that testing trial and suffering. In fact, the Apostle Paul said that Jesus learned by the things that he suffered. A period of proving or a trial of faith is necessary to see if someone who is seeking a special blessing from the Lord will remain faithful in the face of opposition. If a person understands that his faith is going to be tried, it gives him a greater resolve to be persistent in times of opposition.

Your trial of faith basically serves four different functions or purposes. Number one, it determines if a goal you are seeking is truly a desire that you must have, that you need to have. Two, it lets you learn if you are really dedicated to the Lord. Three, it is a means of purging you so that you can become clean, pure, and spotless, literally free from the blood and sins of the world. And four, it humbles you and brings you to the realization that you cannot rely on the arm of flesh.

As you learn to endure your trials of faith, you will literally become a new creature in Christ and your body will be cleansed of all sin and renewed by the Spirit of the Lord. This is, elders and sisters, the process of rebirth and sanctification. And so you see, without opposition and trials, we literally cannot become born again. It is extremely important that you realize that trials of faith are a necessary part of the sanctification process by which we are purified by the Spirit of God.

These verses from the scriptures are interesting. This is from 3 Nephi chapter 24: "and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness." This from the Doctrine and Covenants: "Therefore, they must needs be chastened and tried, even as Abraham, who was commanded to offer up his only son; for all those who will not endure chastening, but deny me, cannot be sanctified." This from Helaman chapter 3, verse 35: "Nevertheless they did fast and pray oft, and did wax stronger and stronger in their humility, and firmer and firmer in the faith of Christ, unto the filling their souls with joy and consolation, yea, even to the purifying and the sanctification of their hearts, which sanctification cometh because of their yielding their hearts unto God."

Opposition plays a very important part in this process. By overcoming opposition and enduring affliction, we are, in a very literal sense, purged and made clean. When you endure opposition by serving the Lord to your utmost ability, no matter how limited your ability is, the grace of God is sufficient to intervene and to add to your limited ability so that you can become perfect in Christ. It is by this means that you actually qualify for the Spirit of the Lord in spite of the limitations of the flesh.

Now, as you consider this, I want you to ask yourself this question: Why does the Lord allow our faith to be tried? Think about that later today, this evening. The nature of a person's individual trial of faith will be based on his particular temperament and disposition. So your trial of faith may be very different than my trial of faith. Your trial of faith can be very different than even your companion's trial of faith because it's suited particularly to you. God knows you better than anyone. He knows you better than you know yourself. And so he knows exactly what is going to test a person's faith and may not test a different person's faith.

This is an interesting scripture: "God will feel after you, and he will take hold of you and wrench your very heartstrings, and if you cannot stand it you will not be fit for an inheritance in the Celestial Kingdom of God." That was Joseph Smith and it was quoted by President Harold B. Lee back in January of 1973.

Your trial of faith will bring you to the realization that you cannot succeed by relying on the, quote, "arm of flesh," close quote. So no matter how strong you are, no matter how strong others are who are trying to help you, it will not be enough to actually bring you to the great desires of your heart. By yourself you are extremely limited in being able to accomplish your truly powerful righteous desires. However, when you humble yourself, fully realizing that you cannot succeed without the Lord's help and submit yourself to your Father in Heaven and become very earnest in your desires, he will extend himself to you.

Every man, every woman can endure their trial of faith whatever it may be by simply remaining faithful and obedient in spite of the opposition, the inconvenience, the discomfort, or the pain. The Lord expects you to be patient in affliction. One of the reasons that this experience that we're having in this lockdown is such a refining tool is that you're having to be patient in your afflictions. Now some of you may be rebelling against that and so you're not benefiting from it as much as you could. But most of you are being patient in the afflictions and you're seeing the refining, sanctifying power of God in your lives.

As you are patient in affliction, not complaining about your problems or discomfort, not criticizing, finding fault, or whining about situations constantly—when you are that way, the sanctifying influence of the Holy Ghost comes into your life and begins to refine you, begins to polish you, begins to purify you. Think about it this way: when you talk to others, emphasize the positive aspects of your life circumstance. The ability to endure hardships patiently is a great virtue that is highly valued and respected by the Lord in His children. It will also bring you maturity, stability, and spiritual strength.

Listen to these scriptures. I think you know them, Alma 17:11: "And the Lord said unto them: Go forth among the Lamanites, your brethren, and establish my word; yet ye shall be patient in long-suffering and afflictions, that ye may show forth good examples unto them in me." And this one from the Doctrine and Covenants: "And if thou shouldst be cast into the pit, or into the hands of murderers, and the sentence of death passed upon thee; if thou be cast into the deep; if the billowing surge conspire against thee; if fierce winds become thine enemy; if the heavens gather blackness, and all the elements combine to hedge up the way; and above all, if the very jaws of hell shall gape open the mouth wide after thee, know thou, my son, that all these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good. The Son of Man hath descended below them all. Art thou greater than he?"

As we think about that powerful verse from the 122nd section of the Doctrine and Covenants, we are reminded of the opposition, the suffering, the afflictions that were endured by the Savior patiently, hopefully, and with love. "But we glory in tribulations also," says the Apostle Paul to the Roman saints, "knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope." "For behold, they were naked, and their skins were worn exceedingly because of being bound with strong cords; and they also had suffered hunger, thirst, and all kinds of afflictions; nevertheless they were patient in all their sufferings." You know where that came from, Alma 20:29. That's the brothers and the helpers of Ammon who were just so happened that they went to a more hardened people to preach the gospel.

Here from the Doctrine and Covenants, another example: "For verily I say unto you, blessed is he that keepeth my commandments, whether in life or in death; and he that is faithful in tribulation, the reward of the same is greater in the kingdom of heaven. Ye cannot behold with your natural eyes, for the present time, the design of your God concerning those things which shall come hereafter, and the glory which shall follow after much tribulation. For after much tribulation come the blessings. Wherefore the day cometh that ye shall be crowned with much glory; the hour is not yet, but is nigh at hand."

Elders and sisters, remember this most important principle: if you stay close to the Spirit, you will not be overwhelmed by the trials of your faith. You have the assurance that with the Spirit as your companion, you can resolve all difficulties. Spirituality impels one to conquer difficulties and acquire more and more strength. And here are a couple of questions for you to ponder just to yourself: How will your faith be tried? Have you responded faithfully in the past when you were confronted with trials and tribulation?

If so, congratulations. If not, try to seek the blessings of heaven again. And when the trials come, recognize them for what they are: your opportunity to be purified and cleansed, sanctified and strengthened, and brought into a place where you literally deserve the blessing that you're asking for from the Lord. All right, elders and sisters, that's all for today. Tomorrow we'll finish this section talking about some of the people who have endured great trials and what we can learn from their experience. Hope you have a wonderful night tonight. I hope you really get a good sleep and enjoy the day tomorrow, maximizing this season of your life to grow in strength and wisdom, knowledge and power, and most particularly your ability to endure affliction well, to show the Lord that you can handle the growth process and the literal afflictions that he's given to you to strengthen and bless you. Catch you tomorrow.
